diagnosis: Calibrated HBV with DDS (NSE objective) on 1971-10 to 1997-12 after a one-year warm-up. Full-period daily NSE 0.873, KGE 0.89, r 0.94, PBIAS about +5% (slight overestimation of flow volume). Split-sample check: calibrating on 1971-1984 gave NSE 0.879, and those parameters gave NSE 0.866 on 1985-1997 with nearly the same values. This suggests the parameters are stable and should transfer to 1998-2008. Parameters: FC≈336 mm, LP 0.92 and BETA≈5.4, so the soil is large and responds nonlinearly (runoff is low until the soil is wet), as expected for a clay-rich lowland catchment. K1≈0.16, K2≈0.056, PERC≈0.86, MAXBAS≈4.9 and UZL is low (≈2.9). The snow parameters have little influence, since only about 2% of precipitation falls as snow; CFR and CWH sit at their lower bounds but this does not matter. Weaknesses: the highest flood peaks are underestimated (simulated maximum about 10 vs 12.5 mm/d observed). Summer low flows and the start of autumn wetting-up are likely imperfect because of the soil-moisture threshold. Urban runoff (11% of the area) is not represented explicitly. Confidence in the response and soil parameters is moderate to high; snow parameters are poorly identified.
